newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Suharto wraps up Cambodia tour, heads for Laos.
newsitem.headline: Suharto wraps up Cambodia tour, heads for Laos.

text.p: Indonesian President Suharto wrapped up a three-day visit to Cambodia on Wednesday, bolstering bilateral ties but not yet formalising entry for Cambodia into the ASEAN regional grouping.

"The ties between Cambodia and Indonesia are strengthened further and further, especially the special relations between his majesty King Norodom Sihanouk and President Suharto," Cambodian Foreign Affairs Minister Ung Huot told reporters after Suharto and his delegation flew to Laos.

When asked about Tuesday's comments by Cambodian co-Minister of the Council of Ministers, Sok An, who said Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas had confirmed Cambodia's July entry into the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN), Ung Huot said Cambodia had not received any formal notification.

"What (Alatas) said is that the heads of state in Jakarta in November made a statement saying Cambodia, Laos and Myanmar (Burma) will enter ASEAN simultaneously at a time to be set, and that still stands for ASEAN," Ung Huot said.
Cambodia, Laos and Burma currently hold observer status in ASEAN, which groups Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam and Brunei.

Following Sok An's announcement on Tuesday of Cambodia's entry, Alatas said Indonesia and other ASEAN nations wanted to see Cambodia join the regional body in July but would not confirm that it would be admitted this year.

Diplomats attributed the mixed statements to confusion ahead of Suharto's arrival in Burma. Human rights concerns among some nations have pressured the regional body to rethink Burma's admittance to ASEAN.
Suharto will next visit Laos and then Burma on his three-country swing through southeast Asia.
